Copolymer Composition Analysis

Source: vignettes/copolymer-analysis.Rmd
copolymer-analysis.Rmd

Scope

This vignette uses sec_copolymer, a synthetic dataset with one supplied styrene fraction and one supplied molecular-weight value per sample. The per-slice UV and RI signals can be used to calculate a relative detector response profile. They do not, by themselves, give a mass fraction.

step_sec_composition() requires four detector-response coefficients calibrated from pure-component standards for the selected input basis. The example dataset does not include those calibration results, so the composition calculation below is shown as a template rather than filled with assumed coefficients.

Sample-level composition values 

library(measure)
#> Loading required package: recipes
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

#>     step
library(measure.sec)
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
data(sec_copolymer, package = "measure.sec")

sample_composition <- sec_copolymer |>
  distinct(sample_id, styrene_fraction) |>
  mutate(acrylate_fraction = 1 - styrene_fraction) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(styrene_fraction, acrylate_fraction),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "fraction"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    component = recode(
      component,
      styrene_fraction = "Styrene",
      acrylate_fraction = "Acrylate"
    )
  )

sample_composition
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>    sample_id  component fraction
#>    <chr>      <chr>        <dbl>
#>  1 Copoly-20S Styrene        0.2
#>  2 Copoly-20S Acrylate       0.8
#>  3 Copoly-40S Styrene        0.4
#>  4 Copoly-40S Acrylate       0.6
#>  5 Copoly-60S Styrene        0.6
#>  6 Copoly-60S Acrylate       0.4
#>  7 Copoly-80S Styrene        0.8
#>  8 Copoly-80S Acrylate       0.2
#>  9 PS-Homo    Styrene        1  
#> 10 PS-Homo    Acrylate       0  
#> 11 PA-Homo    Styrene        0  
#> 12 PA-Homo    Acrylate       1

The bars use the sample-level fraction fields supplied with the synthetic dataset. They do not show slice-level composition recovered from the detector signals.

ggplot(
  sample_composition,
  aes(x = sample_id, y = fraction, fill = component)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Styrene = "#A23B72", Acrylate = "#2E86AB")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Supplied sample-level fraction",
    fill = "Component"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

Sample-level styrene and acrylate fractions supplied with the synthetic dataset. Acrylate is shown as the complement of the supplied styrene fraction.

UV/RI response profiles

step_sec_uv_ri_ratio() retains a relative UV-to-RI response curve. Baseline correction is applied before calculating the ratio. The step sets ratios to NA where the RI signal is below its configured signal threshold; the plot keeps those gaps instead of connecting across them.

copolymer_samples <- sec_copolymer |>
  filter(startsWith(sample_id, "Copoly"))

ratio_recipe <- recipe(
  ri_signal + uv_254_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = copolymer_samples
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_254_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = c("ri", "uv")) |>
  step_sec_uv_ri_ratio(
    uv_col = "uv",
    ri_col = "ri",
    smooth = TRUE
  )

ratio_results <- prep(ratio_recipe) |>
  bake(new_data = NULL)

sample_fractions <- copolymer_samples |>
  distinct(sample_id, styrene_fraction)

ratio_data <- ratio_results |>
  select(sample_id, uv_ri_ratio) |>
  unnest(uv_ri_ratio) |>
  left_join(sample_fractions, by = "sample_id") |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  mutate(segment = cumsum(is.na(value))) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ungroup()

head(ratio_data)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   sample_id  location value styrene_fraction segment
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <dbl>            <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 Copoly-20S     8.02  4.24              0.2       1
#> 2 Copoly-20S     8.24  2.20              0.2      11
#> 3 Copoly-20S     8.34  1.62              0.2      15
#> 4 Copoly-20S     8.36  1.62              0.2      15
#> 5 Copoly-20S     8.48  3.72              0.2      20
#> 6 Copoly-20S     8.6   2.74              0.2      25
ggplot(
  ratio_data,
  aes(
    x = location,
    y = value,
    colour = sample_id,
    group = interaction(sample_id, segment)
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "UV 254 nm / RI detector-response ratio",
    colour = "Sample"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Baseline-corrected UV-to-RI detector-response ratios calculated by step_sec_uv_ri_ratio() for the four synthetic copolymer samples. The ratio is not calibrated to a mass fraction.

The ratio uses the native detector-response basis. Its magnitude depends on the detector channels and their calibration. A changing profile can be investigated as possible compositional variation, but interpreting it as composition requires response calibration and suitable detector alignment.

Calculating component mass fractions

Use step_sec_composition() after measuring the four response coefficients from pure-component standards on the same instrument and with the same signal basis. The code below leaves those measured values as inputs because they are not supplied by sec_copolymer.

composition_recipe <- recipe(
  ri_signal + uv_254_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = copolymer_samples
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_254_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = c("ri", "uv")) |>
  step_sec_composition(
    uv_col = "uv",
    ri_col = "ri",
    component_a_uv = styrene_uv_response,
    component_a_ri = styrene_ri_response,
    component_b_uv = acrylate_uv_response,
    component_b_ri = acrylate_ri_response,
    output_col = "styrene_fraction"
  )

The response coefficients must describe measured detector outputs per concentration for the selected basis. Literature extinction coefficients or dn/dc values alone do not supply these instrument-specific coefficients.

The mw column in sec_copolymer is a supplied sample-level value, repeated across the elution-time rows. It is not a calibrated per-slice molecular-weight curve, so these examples do not plot within-sample composition against MW.
